flags.doc: Output the results unordered (no), dependency-ordered (deps), or fully ordered (full). The default is 'auto', meaning that results are output either dependency-ordered or fully ordered, depending on the output formatter (dependency-ordered for proto, minrank, maxrank, and graph, fully ordered for all others). When output is fully ordered, nodes are printed in a fully deterministic (total) order. First, all nodes are sorted alphabetically. Then, each node in the list is used as the start of a post-order depth-first search in which outgoing edges to unvisited nodes are traversed in alphabetical order of the successor nodes. Finally, nodes are printed in the reverse of the order in which they were visited.

flags.name: order_results
flags.doc: Output the results in dependency-ordered (default) or unordered fashion. The unordered output is faster but only supported when --output is not minrank, maxrank, or graph.

flags.name: output
flags.doc: The format in which the aquery results should be printed. Allowed values for aquery are: text, textproto, proto, streamed_proto, jsonproto.

flags.name: output_base
flags.doc: If set, specifies the output location to which all build output will be written. Otherwise, the location will be ${OUTPUT_ROOT}/_blaze_${USER}/${MD5_OF_WORKSPACE_ROOT}. Note: If you specify a different option from one to the next Bazel invocation for this value, you'll likely start up a new, additional Bazel server. Bazel starts exactly one server per specified output base. Typically there is one output base per workspace - however, with this option you may have multiple output bases per workspace and thereby run multiple builds for the same client on the same machine concurrently. See 'bazel help shutdown' on how to shutdown a Bazel server.

flags.name: output_file
flags.doc: When specified, query results will be written directly to this file, and nothing will be printed to Bazel's standard output stream (stdout). In benchmarks, this is generally faster than bazel query > file.

flags.name: output_filter
flags.doc: Only shows warnings and action outputs for rules with a name matching the provided regular expression.

flags.name: output_groups
flags.doc: A list of comma-separated output group names, each of which optionally prefixed by a + or a -. A group prefixed by + is added to the default set of output groups, while a group prefixed by - is removed from the default set. If at least one group is not prefixed, the default set of output groups is omitted. For example, --output_groups=+foo,+bar builds the union of the default set, foo, and bar, while --output_groups=foo,bar overrides the default set such that only foo and bar are built.

flags.name: output_library_merged_assets
flags.doc: If disabled, does not produce merged asset.zip outputs for library targets

flags.name: output_tree_tracking
flags.doc: If set, tell the output service (if any) to track when files in the output tree have been modified externally (not by the build system). This should improve incremental build speed when an appropriate output service is enabled.

flags.name: output_user_root
flags.doc: The user-specific directory beneath which all build outputs are written; by default, this is a function of $USER, but by specifying a constant, build outputs can be shared between collaborating users.

flags.name: override_module
flags.doc: Override a module with a local path in the form of <module name>=<path>. If the given path is an absolute path, it will be used as it is. If the given path is a relative path, it is relative to the current working directory. If the given path starts with '%workspace%, it is relative to the workspace root, which is the output of `bazel info workspace`. If the given path is empty, then remove any previous overrides.

flags.name: override_repository
flags.doc: Override a repository with a local path in the form of <repository name>=<path>. If the given path is an absolute path, it will be used as it is. If the given path is a relative path, it is relative to the current working directory. If the given path starts with '%workspace%, it is relative to the workspace root, which is the output of `bazel info workspace`. If the given path is empty, then remove any previous overrides.

flags.name: package_path
flags.doc: A colon-separated list of where to look for packages. Elements beginning with '%workspace%' are relative to the enclosing workspace. If omitted or empty, the default is the output of 'bazel info default-package-path'.

flags.name: packages
flags.doc: Dump package cache content.

flags.name: per_file_copt
flags.doc: Additional options to selectively pass to gcc when compiling certain files. This option can be passed multiple times. Syntax: regex_filter@option_1,option_2,...,option_n. Where regex_filter stands for a list of include and exclude regular expression patterns (Also see --instrumentation_filter). option_1 to option_n stand for arbitrary command line options. If an option contains a comma it has to be quoted with a backslash. Options can contain @. Only the first @ is used to split the string. Example: --per_file_copt=//foo/.*\.cc,-//foo/bar\.cc@-O0 adds the -O0 command line option to the gcc command line of all cc files in //foo/ except bar.cc.

flags.name: per_file_ltobackendopt
flags.doc: Additional options to selectively pass to LTO backend (under --features=thin_lto) when compiling certain backend objects. This option can be passed multiple times. Syntax: regex_filter@option_1,option_2,...,option_n. Where regex_filter stands for a list of include and exclude regular expression patterns. option_1 to option_n stand for arbitrary command line options. If an option contains a comma it has to be quoted with a backslash. Options can contain @. Only the first @ is used to split the string. Example: --per_file_ltobackendopt=//foo/.*\.o,-//foo/bar\.o@-O0 adds the -O0 command line option to the LTO backend command line of all o files in //foo/ except bar.o.

flags.name: persistent_android_dex_desugar
flags.doc: Enable persistent Android dex and desugar actions by using workers.

flags.name: persistent_android_resource_processor
flags.doc: Enable persistent Android resource processor by using workers.

flags.name: persistent_multiplex_android_dex_desugar
flags.doc: Enable persistent multiplexed Android dex and desugar actions by using workers.

flags.name: persistent_multiplex_android_resource_processor
flags.doc: Enable persistent multiplexed Android resource processor by using workers.

flags.name: persistent_multiplex_android_tools
flags.doc: Enable persistent and multiplexed Android tools (dexing, desugaring, resource processing).

flags.name: platform_mappings
flags.doc: The location of a mapping file that describes which platform to use if none is set or which flags to set when a platform already exists. Must be relative to the main workspace root. Defaults to 'platform_mappings' (a file directly under the workspace root).

flags.name: platform_suffix
flags.doc: Specifies a suffix to be added to the configuration directory.

flags.name: platforms
flags.doc: The labels of the platform rules describing the target platforms for the current command.

flags.name: plugin
flags.doc: Plugins to use in the build. Currently works with java_plugin.

flags.name: preemptible
flags.doc: If true, the command can be preempted if another command is started.

flags.name: print_action_mnemonics
flags.doc: Lists which mnemonics to filter print_action data by, no filtering takes place when left empty.

flags.name: print_relative_test_log_paths
flags.doc: If true, when printing the path to a test log, use relative path that makes use of the 'testlogs' convenience symlink. N.B. - A subsequent 'build'/'test'/etc invocation with a different configuration can cause the target of this symlink to change, making the path printed previously no longer useful.

flags.name: process_headers_in_dependencies
flags.doc: When building a target //a:a, process headers in all targets that //a:a depends on (if header processing is enabled for the toolchain).

flags.name: product_name
flags.doc: The name of the build system. It is used as part of the name of the generated directories (e.g. productName-bin for binaries) as well as for printing error messages and logging

flags.name: profile
flags.doc: If set, profile Bazel and write data to the specified file. Use bazel analyze-profile to analyze the profile.

flags.name: progress_in_terminal_title
flags.doc: Show the command progress in the terminal title. Useful to see what bazel is doing when having multiple terminal tabs.

flags.name: progress_report_interval
flags.doc: The number of seconds to wait between reports on still running jobs. The default value 0 means the first report will be printed after 10 seconds, then 30 seconds and after that progress is reported once every minute. When --curses is enabled, progress is reported every second.

flags.name: proguard_top
flags.doc: Specifies which version of ProGuard to use for code removal when building a Java binary.

flags.name: propeller_optimize
flags.doc: Use Propeller profile information to optimize the build target.A propeller profile must consist of at least one of two files, a cc profile and a ld profile.  This flag accepts a build label which must refer to the propeller profile input files. For example, the BUILD file that defines the label, in a/b/BUILD:propeller_optimize(    name = "propeller_profile",    cc_profile = "propeller_cc_profile.txt",    ld_profile = "propeller_ld_profile.txt",)An exports_files directive may have to be added to the corresponding package to make these files visible to Bazel. The option must be used as: --propeller_optimize=//a/b:propeller_profile

flags.name: propeller_optimize_absolute_cc_profile
flags.doc: Absolute path name of cc_profile file for Propeller Optimized builds.

flags.name: propeller_optimize_absolute_ld_profile
flags.doc: Absolute path name of ld_profile file for Propeller Optimized builds.

flags.name: proto_compiler
flags.doc: The label of the proto-compiler.

flags.name: proto_toolchain_for_cc
flags.doc: Label of proto_lang_toolchain() which describes how to compile C++ protos

flags.name: proto_toolchain_for_j2objc
flags.doc: Label of proto_lang_toolchain() which describes how to compile j2objc protos

flags.name: proto_toolchain_for_java
flags.doc: Label of proto_lang_toolchain() which describes how to compile Java protos

flags.name: proto_toolchain_for_javalite
flags.doc: Label of proto_lang_toolchain() which describes how to compile JavaLite protos

flags.name: proto:default_values
flags.doc: If true, attributes whose value is not explicitly specified in the BUILD file are included; otherwise they are omitted. This option is applicable to --output=proto

flags.name: proto:definition_stack
flags.doc: Populate the definition_stack proto field, which records for each rule instance the Starlark call stack at the moment the rule's class was defined.

flags.name: proto:flatten_selects
flags.doc: If enabled, configurable attributes created by select() are flattened. For list types the flattened representation is a list containing each value of the select map exactly once. Scalar types are flattened to null.

flags.name: proto:include_attribute_source_aspects
flags.doc: Populate the source_aspect_name proto field of each Attribute with the source aspect that the attribute came from (empty string if it did not).

flags.name: proto:include_configurations
flags.doc: if enabled, proto output will include information about configurations. When disabled,cquery proto output format resembles query output format.

flags.name: proto:include_synthetic_attribute_hash
flags.doc: Whether or not to calculate and populate the $internal_attr_hash attribute.

flags.name: proto:instantiation_stack
flags.doc: Populate the instantiation call stack of each rule. Note that this requires the stack to be present

flags.name: proto:locations
flags.doc: Whether to output location information in proto output at all.

flags.name: proto:output_rule_attrs
flags.doc: Comma separated list of attributes to include in output. Defaults to all attributes. Set to empty string to not output any attribute. This option is applicable to --output=proto.

flags.name: proto:rule_inputs_and_outputs
flags.doc: Whether or not to populate the rule_input and rule_output fields.

flags.name: protocopt
flags.doc: Additional options to pass to the protobuf compiler.

flags.name: python_native_rules_allowlist
flags.doc: An allowlist (package_group target) to use when enforcing --incompatible_python_disallow_native_rules.

flags.name: python_path
flags.doc: The absolute path of the Python interpreter invoked to run Python targets on the target platform. Deprecated; disabled by --incompatible_use_python_toolchains.

flags.name: python_top
flags.doc: The label of a py_runtime representing the Python interpreter invoked to run Python targets on the target platform. Deprecated; disabled by --incompatible_use_python_toolchains.

flags.name: python_version
flags.doc: The Python major version mode, either `PY2` or `PY3`. Note that this is overridden by `py_binary` and `py_test` targets (even if they don't explicitly specify a version) so there is usually not much reason to supply this flag.

flags.name: python2_path
flags.doc: Deprecated, no-op. Disabled by `--incompatible_use_python_toolchains`.

flags.name: python3_path
flags.doc: Deprecated, no-op. Disabled by `--incompatible_use_python_toolchains`.

flags.name: query_file
flags.doc: If set, query will read the query from the file named here, rather than on the command line. It is an error to specify a file here as well as a command-line query.

flags.name: record_full_profiler_data
flags.doc: By default, Bazel profiler will record only aggregated data for fast but numerous events (such as statting the file). If this option is enabled, profiler will record each event - resulting in more precise profiling data but LARGE performance hit. Option only has effect if --profile used as well.

flags.name: record_metrics_for_all_packages
flags.doc: Configures PackageMetrics to record all metrics for all packages. Disables Top-n INFO logging.

flags.name: registry
flags.doc: Specifies the registries to use to locate Bazel module dependencies. The order is important: modules will be looked up in earlier registries first, and only fall back to later registries when they're missing from the earlier ones.

flags.name: relative_locations
flags.doc: If true, the location of BUILD files in xml and proto outputs will be relative. By default, the location output is an absolute path and will not be consistent across machines. You can set this option to true to have a consistent result across machines.

flags.name: remote_accept_cached
flags.doc: Whether to accept remotely cached action results.

flags.name: remote_build_event_upload
flags.doc:
If set to 'all', all local outputs referenced by BEP are uploaded to remote cache.
If set to 'minimal', local outputs referenced by BEP are not uploaded to the remote cache, except for files that are important to the consumers of BEP (e.g. test logs and timing profile). bytestream:// scheme is always used for the uri of files even if they are missing from remote cache.
Default to 'minimal'.

flags.name: remote_bytestream_uri_prefix
flags.doc: The hostname and instance name to be used in bytestream:// URIs that are written into build event streams. This option can be set when builds are performed using a proxy, which causes the values of --remote_executor and --remote_instance_name to no longer correspond to the canonical name of the remote execution service. When not set, it will default to "${hostname}/${instance_name}".

flags.name: remote_cache
flags.doc: A URI of a caching endpoint. The supported schemas are http, https, grpc, grpcs (grpc with TLS enabled) and unix (local UNIX sockets). If no schema is provided Bazel will default to grpcs. Specify grpc://, http:// or unix: schema to disable TLS. See https://bazel.build/remote/caching

flags.name: remote_cache_compression
flags.doc: If enabled, compress/decompress cache blobs with zstd when their size is at least --experimental_remote_cache_compression_threshold.

flags.name: remote_cache_header
flags.doc: Specify a header that will be included in cache requests: --remote_cache_header=Name=Value. Multiple headers can be passed by specifying the flag multiple times. Multiple values for the same name will be converted to a comma-separated list.

flags.name: remote_default_exec_properties
flags.doc: Set the default exec properties to be used as the remote execution platform if an execution platform does not already set exec_properties.

flags.name: remote_default_platform_properties
flags.doc: Set the default platform properties to be set for the remote execution API, if the execution platform does not already set remote_execution_properties. This value will also be used if the host platform is selected as the execution platform for remote execution.

flags.name: remote_download_all
flags.doc: Downloads all remote outputs to the local machine. This flag is an alias for --remote_download_outputs=all.

flags.name: remote_download_minimal
flags.doc: Does not download any remote build outputs to the local machine. This flag is an alias for --remote_download_outputs=minimal.

flags.name: remote_download_outputs
flags.doc: If set to 'minimal' doesn't download any remote build outputs to the local machine, except the ones required by local actions. If set to 'toplevel' behaves like'minimal' except that it also downloads outputs of top level targets to the local machine. Both options can significantly reduce build times if network bandwidth is a bottleneck.

flags.name: remote_download_regex
flags.doc: Force remote build outputs whose path matches this pattern to be downloaded, irrespective of --remote_download_outputs. Multiple patterns may be specified by repeating this flag.

flags.name: remote_download_symlink_template
flags.doc: Instead of downloading remote build outputs to the local machine, create symbolic links. The target of the symbolic links can be specified in the form of a template string. This template string may contain {hash} and {size_bytes} that expand to the hash of the object and the size in bytes, respectively. These symbolic links may, for example, point to a FUSE file system that loads objects from the CAS on demand.

flags.name: remote_download_toplevel
flags.doc: Only downloads remote outputs of top level targets to the local machine. This flag is an alias for --remote_download_outputs=toplevel.

flags.name: remote_downloader_header
flags.doc: Specify a header that will be included in remote downloader requests: --remote_downloader_header=Name=Value. Multiple headers can be passed by specifying the flag multiple times. Multiple values for the same name will be converted to a comma-separated list.

flags.name: remote_exec_header
flags.doc: Specify a header that will be included in execution requests: --remote_exec_header=Name=Value. Multiple headers can be passed by specifying the flag multiple times. Multiple values for the same name will be converted to a comma-separated list.

flags.name: remote_execution_priority
flags.doc: The relative priority of actions to be executed remotely. The semantics of the particular priority values are server-dependent.

flags.name: remote_executor
flags.doc: HOST or HOST:PORT of a remote execution endpoint. The supported schemas are grpc, grpcs (grpc with TLS enabled) and unix (local UNIX sockets). If no schema is provided Bazel will default to grpcs. Specify grpc:// or unix: schema to disable TLS.

flags.name: remote_grpc_log
flags.doc: If specified, a path to a file to log gRPC call related details. This log consists of a sequence of serialized com.google.devtools.build.lib.remote.logging.RemoteExecutionLog.LogEntry protobufs with each message prefixed by a varint denoting the size of the following serialized protobuf message, as performed by the method LogEntry.writeDelimitedTo(OutputStream).

flags.name: remote_header
flags.doc: Specify a header that will be included in requests: --remote_header=Name=Value. Multiple headers can be passed by specifying the flag multiple times. Multiple values for the same name will be converted to a comma-separated list.

flags.name: remote_instance_name
flags.doc: Value to pass as instance_name in the remote execution API.

flags.name: remote_local_fallback
flags.doc: Whether to fall back to standalone local execution strategy if remote execution fails.

flags.name: remote_local_fallback_strategy
flags.doc: No-op, deprecated. See https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/7480 for details.

flags.name: remote_max_connections
flags.doc:
Limit the max number of concurrent connections to remote cache/executor. By default the value is 100. Setting this to 0 means no limitation.
For HTTP remote cache, one TCP connection could handle one request at one time, so Bazel could make up to --remote_max_connections concurrent requests.
For gRPC remote cache/executor, one gRPC channel could usually handle 100+ concurrent requests, so Bazel could make around `--remote_max_connections * 100` concurrent requests.

flags.name: remote_print_execution_messages
flags.doc: Choose when to print remote execution messages. Valid values are `failure`, to print only on failures, `success` to print only on successes and `all` to print always.

flags.name: remote_proxy
flags.doc: Connect to the remote cache through a proxy. Currently this flag can only be used to configure a Unix domain socket (unix:/path/to/socket).

flags.name: remote_result_cache_priority
flags.doc: The relative priority of remote actions to be stored in remote cache. The semantics of the particular priority values are server-dependent.

flags.name: remote_retries
flags.doc: The maximum number of attempts to retry a transient error. If set to 0, retries are disabled.

flags.name: remote_retry_max_delay
flags.doc: The maximum backoff delay between remote retry attempts. Following units can be used: Days (d), hours (h), minutes (m), seconds (s), and milliseconds (ms). If the unit is omitted, the value is interpreted as seconds.

flags.name: remote_timeout
flags.doc: The maximum amount of time to wait for remote execution and cache calls. For the REST cache, this is both the connect and the read timeout. Following units can be used: Days (d), hours (h), minutes (m), seconds (s), and milliseconds (ms). If the unit is omitted, the value is interpreted as seconds.

flags.name: remote_upload_local_results
flags.doc: Whether to upload locally executed action results to the remote cache if the remote cache supports it and the user is authorized to do so.

flags.name: remote_verify_downloads
flags.doc: If set to true, Bazel will compute the hash sum of all remote downloads and  discard the remotely cached values if they don't match the expected value.

flags.name: repo
flags.doc: Only fetches the specified repository, which can be either {@apparent_repo_name} or {@@canonical_repo_name}. Only works when --enable_bzlmod is on.

flags.name: repo_env
flags.doc: Specifies additional environment variables to be available only for repository rules. Note that repository rules see the full environment anyway, but in this way configuration information can be passed to repositories through options without invalidating the action graph.

flags.name: repositories_without_autoloads
flags.doc: A list of additional repositories (beyond the hardcoded ones Bazel knows about) where autoloads are not to be added. This should typically contain repositories that are transitively depended on by a repository that may be loaded automatically (and which can therefore potentially create a cycle).

flags.name: repository_cache
flags.doc: Specifies the cache location of the downloaded values obtained during the fetching of external repositories. An empty string as argument requests the cache to be disabled, otherwise the default of '<output_user_root>/cache/repos/v1' is used

flags.name: repository_disable_download
flags.doc: If set, downloading using ctx.download{,_and_extract} is not allowed during repository fetching. Note that network access is not completely disabled; ctx.execute could still run an arbitrary executable that accesses the Internet.

flags.name: restart_reason
flags.doc: The reason for the server restart.

flags.name: reuse_sandbox_directories
flags.doc: If set to true, directories used by sandboxed non-worker execution may be reused to avoid unnecessary setup costs.

flags.name: rewind_lost_inputs
flags.doc: Whether to use action rewinding to recover from lost inputs. Ignored unless prerequisites for rewinding are met (no incrementality, no action cache).

flags.name: rule_classes
flags.doc: Dump rule classes.

flags.name: rules
flags.doc: Dump rules, including counts and memory usage (if memory is tracked).

flags.name: run
flags.doc: If false, skip running the command line constructed for the built target.

flags.name: run_under
flags.doc: Prefix to insert before the executables for the 'test' and 'run' commands. If the value is 'foo -bar', and the execution command line is 'test_binary -baz', then the final command line is 'foo -bar test_binary -baz'.This can also be a label to an executable target. Some examples are: 'valgrind', 'strace', 'strace -c', 'valgrind --quiet --num-callers=20', '//package:target',  '//package:target --options'.

flags.name: run_validations
flags.doc: Whether to run validation actions as part of the build. See https://bazel.build/extending/rules#validation_actions

flags.name: runs_per_test
flags.doc: Specifies number of times to run each test. If any of those attempts fail for any reason, the whole test is considered failed. Normally the value specified is just an integer. Example: --runs_per_test=3 will run all tests 3 times. Alternate syntax: regex_filter@runs_per_test. Where runs_per_test stands for an integer value and regex_filter stands for a list of include and exclude regular expression patterns (Also see --instrumentation_filter). Example: --runs_per_test=//foo/.*,-//foo/bar/.*@3 runs all tests in //foo/ except those under foo/bar three times. This option can be passed multiple times. The most recently passed argument that matches takes precedence. If nothing matches, the test is only run once.

flags.name: runs_per_test_detects_flakes
flags.doc: If true, any shard in which at least one run/attempt passes and at least one run/attempt fails gets a FLAKY status.

flags.name: sandbox_add_mount_pair
flags.doc: Add additional path pair to mount in sandbox.

flags.name: sandbox_base
flags.doc: Lets the sandbox create its sandbox directories underneath this path. Specify a path on tmpfs (like /run/shm) to possibly improve performance a lot when your build / tests have many input files. Note: You need enough RAM and free space on the tmpfs to hold output and intermediate files generated by running actions.

flags.name: sandbox_block_path
flags.doc: For sandboxed actions, disallow access to this path.

flags.name: sandbox_debug
flags.doc: Enables debugging features for the sandboxing feature. This includes two things: first, the sandbox root contents are left untouched after a build; and second, prints extra debugging information on execution. This can help developers of Bazel or Starlark rules with debugging failures due to missing input files, etc.

flags.name: sandbox_default_allow_network
flags.doc: Allow network access by default for actions; this may not work with all sandboxing implementations.

flags.name: sandbox_explicit_pseudoterminal
flags.doc: Explicitly enable the creation of pseudoterminals for sandboxed actions. Some linux distributions require setting the group id of the process to 'tty' inside the sandbox in order for pseudoterminals to function. If this is causing issues, this flag can be disabled to enable other groups to be used.

flags.name: sandbox_fake_hostname
flags.doc: Change the current hostname to 'localhost' for sandboxed actions.

flags.name: sandbox_fake_username
flags.doc: Change the current username to 'nobody' for sandboxed actions.

flags.name: sandbox_tmpfs_path
flags.doc: For sandboxed actions, mount an empty, writable directory at this absolute path (if supported by the sandboxing implementation, ignored otherwise).

flags.name: sandbox_writable_path
flags.doc: For sandboxed actions, make an existing directory writable in the sandbox (if supported by the sandboxing implementation, ignored otherwise).

flags.name: save_temps
flags.doc: If set, temporary outputs from gcc will be saved.  These include .s files (assembler code), .i files (preprocessed C) and .ii files (preprocessed C++).

flags.name: script_path
flags.doc: If set, write a shell script to the given file which invokes the target. If this option is set, the target is not run from %{product}. Use '%{product} run --script_path=foo //foo && ./foo' to invoke target '//foo' This differs from '%{product} run //foo' in that the %{product} lock is released and the executable is connected to the terminal's stdin.

flags.name: server_javabase
flags.doc: Path to the JVM used to execute Bazel itself.

flags.name: server_jvm_out
flags.doc: The location to write the server's JVM's output. If unset then defaults to a location in output_base.

flags.name: share_native_deps
flags.doc: If true, native libraries that contain identical functionality will be shared among different targets

flags.name: shell_executable
flags.doc: Absolute path to the shell executable for Bazel to use. If this is unset, but the BAZEL_SH environment variable is set on the first Bazel invocation (that starts up a Bazel server), Bazel uses that. If neither is set, Bazel uses a hard-coded default path depending on the operating system it runs on (Windows: c:/tools/msys64/usr/bin/bash.exe, FreeBSD: /usr/local/bin/bash, all others: /bin/bash). Note that using a shell that is not compatible with bash may lead to build failures or runtime failures of the generated binaries.

flags.name: short
flags.doc: Show only the names of the options, not their types or meanings.

flags.name: show_config_fragments
flags.doc: Shows the configuration fragments required by a rule and its transitive dependencies. This can be useful for evaluating how much a configured target graph can be trimmed.

flags.name: show_loading_progress
flags.doc: If enabled, causes Bazel to print "Loading package:" messages.

flags.name: show_make_env
flags.doc: Include the "Make" environment in the output.

flags.name: show_progress
flags.doc: Display progress messages during a build.

flags.name: show_progress_rate_limit
flags.doc: Minimum number of seconds between progress messages in the output.

flags.name: show_result
flags.doc:
Show the results of the build.  For each target, state whether or not it was brought up-to-date, and if so, a list of output files that were built.  The printed files are convenient strings for copy+pasting to the shell, to execute them.
This option requires an integer argument, which is the threshold number of targets above which result information is not printed. Thus zero causes suppression of the message and MAX_INT causes printing of the result to occur always. The default is one.
If nothing was built for a target its results may be omitted to keep the output under the threshold.

flags.name: show_timestamps
flags.doc: Include timestamps in messages

flags.name: shutdown_on_low_sys_mem
flags.doc: If max_idle_secs is set and the build server has been idle for a while, shut down the server when the system is low on free RAM. Linux only.

flags.name: skip_incompatible_explicit_targets
flags.doc: Skip incompatible targets that are explicitly listed on the command line. By default, building such targets results in an error but they are silently skipped when this option is enabled. See: https://bazel.build/extending/platforms#skipping-incompatible-targets

flags.name: skyframe
flags.doc: Dump Skyframe graph: 'off', 'summary', 'count', 'deps', or 'rdeps'.

flags.name: skyframe_high_water_mark_full_gc_drops_per_invocation
flags.doc: Flag for advanced configuration of Bazel's internal Skyframe engine. If Bazel detects its retained heap percentage usage exceeds the threshold set by --skyframe_high_water_mark_threshold, when a full GC event occurs, it will drop unnecessary temporary Skyframe state, up to this many times per invocation. Defaults to Integer.MAX_VALUE; effectively unlimited. Zero means that full GC events will never trigger drops. If the limit is reached, Skyframe state will no longer be dropped when a full GC event occurs and that retained heap percentage threshold is exceeded.

flags.name: skyframe_high_water_mark_minor_gc_drops_per_invocation
flags.doc: Flag for advanced configuration of Bazel's internal Skyframe engine. If Bazel detects its retained heap percentage usage exceeds the threshold set by --skyframe_high_water_mark_threshold, when a minor GC event occurs, it will drop unnecessary temporary Skyframe state, up to this many times per invocation. Defaults to Integer.MAX_VALUE; effectively unlimited. Zero means that minor GC events will never trigger drops. If the limit is reached, Skyframe state will no longer be dropped when a minor GC event occurs and that retained heap percentage threshold is exceeded.

flags.name: skyframe_high_water_mark_threshold
flags.doc: Flag for advanced configuration of Bazel's internal Skyframe engine. If Bazel detects its retained heap percentage usage is at least this threshold, it will drop unnecessary temporary Skyframe state. Tweaking this may let you mitigate wall time impact of GC thrashing, when the GC thrashing is (i) caused by the memory usage of this temporary state and (ii) more costly than reconstituting the state when it is needed.

flags.name: skyframe_state
flags.doc: Without performing extra analysis, dump the current Action Graph from Skyframe. Note: Specifying a target with --skyframe_state is currently not supported. This flag is only available with --output=proto or --output=textproto.

flags.name: skykey_filter
flags.doc: Regex filter of SkyKey names to output. Only used with --skyframe=deps, rdeps.

flags.name: skylark_memory
flags.doc: Dumps a pprof-compatible memory profile to the specified path. To learn more please see https://github.com/google/pprof.

flags.name: slim_profile
flags.doc: Slims down the size of the JSON profile by merging events if the profile gets  too large.

flags.name: spawn_strategy
flags.doc: Specify how spawn actions are executed by default. Accepts a comma-separated list of strategies from highest to lowest priority. For each action Bazel picks the strategy with the highest priority that can execute the action. The default value is "remote,worker,sandboxed,local". See https://blog.bazel.build/2019/06/19/list-strategy.html for details.

flags.name: split_apks
flags.doc: Whether to use split apks to install and update the application on the device. Works only with devices with Marshmallow or later

flags.name: split_bytecode_optimization_pass
flags.doc: Do not use.

flags.name: stamp
flags.doc: Stamp binaries with the date, username, hostname, workspace information, etc.

flags.name: starlark_cpu_profile
flags.doc: Writes into the specified file a pprof profile of CPU usage by all Starlark threads.

flags.name: starlark:expr
flags.doc: A Starlark expression to format each configured target in cquery's --output=starlark mode. The configured target is bound to 'target'. If neither --starlark:expr nor --starlark:file is specified, this option will default to 'str(target.label)'. It is an error to specify both --starlark:expr and --starlark:file.

flags.name: starlark:file
flags.doc: The name of a file that defines a Starlark function called 'format', of one argument, that is applied to each configured target to format it as a string. It is an error to specify both --starlark:expr and --starlark:file. See help for --output=starlark for additional detail.

flags.name: start
flags.doc: How the app should be started after installing it. Set to WARM to preserve and restore application state on incremental installs.

flags.name: start_app
flags.doc: Whether to start the app after installing it.

flags.name: start_end_lib
flags.doc: Use the --start-lib/--end-lib ld options if supported by the toolchain.

flags.name: startup_time
flags.doc: The time in ms the launcher spends before sending the request to the bazel server.

flags.name: strategy
flags.doc: Specify how to distribute compilation of other spawn actions. Accepts a comma-separated list of strategies from highest to lowest priority. For each action Bazel picks the strategy with the highest priority that can execute the action. The default value is "remote,worker,sandboxed,local". This flag overrides the values set by --spawn_strategy (and --genrule_strategy if used with mnemonic Genrule). See https://blog.bazel.build/2019/06/19/list-strategy.html for details.

flags.name: strategy_regexp
flags.doc: Override which spawn strategy should be used to execute spawn actions that have descriptions matching a certain regex_filter. See --per_file_copt for details onregex_filter matching. The last regex_filter that matches the description is used. This option overrides other flags for specifying strategy. Example: --strategy_regexp=//foo.*\.cc,-//foo/bar=local means to run actions using local strategy if their descriptions match //foo.*.cc but not //foo/bar. Example: --strategy_regexp='Compiling.*/bar=local  --strategy_regexp=Compiling=sandboxed will run 'Compiling //foo/bar/baz' with the 'local' strategy, but reversing the order would run it with 'sandboxed'.

flags.name: strict_deps_java_protos
flags.doc: When 'strict-deps' is on, .java files that depend on classes not declared in their rule's 'deps' fail to build. In other words, it's forbidden to depend on classes obtained transitively. When true, Java protos are strict regardless of their 'strict_deps' attribute.

flags.name: strict_filesets
flags.doc: If this option is enabled, filesets crossing package boundaries are reported as errors.

flags.name: strict_proto_deps
flags.doc: Unless OFF, checks that a proto_library target explicitly declares all directly used targets as dependencies.

flags.name: strict_public_imports
flags.doc: Unless OFF, checks that a proto_library target explicitly declares all targets used in 'import public' as exported.

flags.name: strict_system_includes
flags.doc: If true, headers found through system include paths (-isystem) are also required to be declared.

flags.name: strict_test_suite
flags.doc: If true, the tests() expression gives an error if it encounters a test_suite containing non-test targets.

flags.name: strip
flags.doc: Specifies whether to strip binaries and shared libraries  (using "-Wl,--strip-debug").  The default value of 'sometimes' means strip iff --compilation_mode=fastbuild.

flags.name: stripopt
flags.doc: Additional options to pass to strip when generating a '<name>.stripped' binary.

flags.name: subcommands
flags.doc: Display the subcommands executed during a build. Related flags: --execution_log_json_file, --execution_log_binary_file (for logging subcommands to a file in a tool-friendly format).

flags.name: swiftcopt
flags.doc: Additional options to pass to Swift compilation.

flags.name: symlink_prefix
flags.doc: The prefix that is prepended to any of the convenience symlinks that are created after a build. If omitted, the default value is the name of the build tool followed by a hyphen. If '/' is passed, then no symlinks are created and no warning is emitted. Warning: the special functionality for '/' will be deprecated soon; use --experimental_convenience_symlinks=ignore instead.

flags.name: system_rc
flags.doc: Whether or not to look for the system-wide bazelrc.

flags.name: target_environment
flags.doc: Declares this build's target environment. Must be a label reference to an "environment" rule. If specified, all top-level targets must be compatible with this environment.

flags.name: target_pattern_file
flags.doc: If set, build will read patterns from the file named here, rather than on the command line. It is an error to specify a file here as well as command-line patterns.

flags.name: target_platform_fallback
flags.doc: This option is deprecated and has no effect.

flags.name: terminal_columns
flags.doc: A system-generated parameter which specifies the terminal width in columns.

flags.name: test_arg
flags.doc: Specifies additional options and arguments that should be passed to the test executable. Can be used multiple times to specify several arguments. If multiple tests are executed, each of them will receive identical arguments. Used only by the 'bazel test' command.

flags.name: test_env
flags.doc: Specifies additional environment variables to be injected into the test runner environment. Variables can be either specified by name, in which case its value will be read from the Bazel client environment, or by the name=value pair. This option can be used multiple times to specify several variables. Used only by the 'bazel test' command.

flags.name: test_filter
flags.doc: Specifies a filter to forward to the test framework.  Used to limit the tests run. Note that this does not affect which targets are built.

flags.name: test_keep_going
flags.doc: When disabled, any non-passing test will cause the entire build to stop. By default all tests are run, even if some do not pass.

flags.name: test_lang_filters
flags.doc: Specifies a comma-separated list of test languages. Each language can be optionally preceded with '-' to specify excluded languages. Only those test targets will be found that are written in the specified languages. The name used for each language should be the same as the language prefix in the *_test rule, e.g. one of 'cc', 'java', 'py', etc. This option affects --build_tests_only behavior and the test command.

flags.name: test_output
flags.doc: Specifies desired output mode. Valid values are 'summary' to output only test status summary, 'errors' to also print test logs for failed tests, 'all' to print logs for all tests and 'streamed' to output logs for all tests in real time (this will force tests to be executed locally one at a time regardless of --test_strategy value).

flags.name: test_result_expiration
flags.doc: This option is deprecated and has no effect.

flags.name: test_runner_fail_fast
flags.doc: Forwards fail fast option to the test runner. The test runner should stop execution upon first failure.

flags.name: test_sharding_strategy
flags.doc: Specify strategy for test sharding: 'explicit' to only use sharding if the 'shard_count' BUILD attribute is present. 'disabled' to never use test sharding. 'forced=k' to enforce 'k' shards for testing regardless of the 'shard_count' BUILD attribute.

flags.name: test_size_filters
flags.doc: Specifies a comma-separated list of test sizes. Each size can be optionally preceded with '-' to specify excluded sizes. Only those test targets will be found that contain at least one included size and do not contain any excluded sizes. This option affects --build_tests_only behavior and the test command.

flags.name: test_strategy
flags.doc: Specifies which strategy to use when running tests.

flags.name: test_summary
flags.doc: Specifies the desired format of the test summary. Valid values are 'short' to print information only about tests executed, 'terse', to print information only about unsuccessful tests that were run, 'detailed' to print detailed information about failed test cases, 'testcase' to print summary in test case resolution, do not print detailed information about failed test cases and 'none' to omit the summary.

flags.name: test_tag_filters
flags.doc: Specifies a comma-separated list of test tags. Each tag can be optionally preceded with '-' to specify excluded tags. Only those test targets will be found that contain at least one included tag and do not contain any excluded tags. This option affects --build_tests_only behavior and the test command.

flags.name: test_timeout
flags.doc: Override the default test timeout values for test timeouts (in secs). If a single positive integer value is specified it will override all categories.  If 4 comma-separated integers are specified, they will override the timeouts for short, moderate, long and eternal (in that order). In either form, a value of -1 tells blaze to use its default timeouts for that category.

flags.name: test_timeout_filters
flags.doc: Specifies a comma-separated list of test timeouts. Each timeout can be optionally preceded with '-' to specify excluded timeouts. Only those test targets will be found that contain at least one included timeout and do not contain any excluded timeouts. This option affects --build_tests_only behavior and the test command.

flags.name: test_tmpdir
flags.doc: Specifies the base temporary directory for 'bazel test' to use.

flags.name: test_verbose_timeout_warnings
flags.doc: If true, print additional warnings when the actual test execution time does not match the timeout defined by the test (whether implied or explicit).

flags.name: tls_authority_override
flags.doc: TESTING ONLY! Can be used with a self-signed certificate to consider the specified value a valid TLS authority.

flags.name: tls_certificate
flags.doc: Specify a path to a TLS certificate that is trusted to sign server certificates.

flags.name: tls_client_certificate
flags.doc: Specify the TLS client certificate to use; you also need to provide a client key to enable client authentication.

flags.name: tls_client_key
flags.doc: Specify the TLS client key to use; you also need to provide a client certificate to enable client authentication.

flags.name: tool_deps
flags.doc:
Query: If disabled, dependencies on 'exec configuration' will not be included in the dependency graph over which the query operates. An 'exec configuration' dependency edge, such as the one from any 'proto_library' rule to the Protocol Compiler, usually points to a tool executed during the build rather than a part of the same 'target' program.
Cquery: If disabled, filters out all configured targets which cross an execution transition from the top-level target that discovered this configured target. That means if the top-level target is in the target configuration, only configured targets also in the target configuration will be returned. If the top-level target is in the exec configuration, only exec configured targets will be returned. This option will NOT exclude resolved toolchains.

flags.name: tool_java_language_version
flags.doc: The Java language version used to execute the tools that are needed during a build

flags.name: tool_java_runtime_version
flags.doc: The Java runtime version used to execute tools during the build

flags.name: tool_tag
flags.doc: A tool name to attribute this Bazel invocation to.

flags.name: toolchain_resolution_debug
flags.doc: Print debug information during toolchain resolution. The flag takes a regex, which is checked against toolchain types and specific targets to see which to debug. Multiple regexes may be  separated by commas, and then each regex is checked separately. Note: The output of this flag is very complex and will likely only be useful to experts in toolchain resolution.

flags.name: track_incremental_state
flags.doc: If false, Blaze will not persist data that allows for invalidation and re-evaluation on incremental builds in order to save memory on this build. Subsequent builds will not have any incrementality with respect to this one. Usually you will want to specify --batch when setting this to false.

flags.name: transitions
flags.doc: The format in which cquery will print transition information.

flags.name: trim_test_configuration
flags.doc: When enabled, test-related options will be cleared below the top level of the build. When this flag is active, tests cannot be built as dependencies of non-test rules, but changes to test-related options will not cause non-test rules to be re-analyzed.

flags.name: tvos_cpus
flags.doc: Comma-separated list of architectures for which to build Apple tvOS binaries.

flags.name: tvos_minimum_os
flags.doc: Minimum compatible tvOS version for target simulators and devices. If unspecified, uses 'tvos_sdk_version'.

flags.name: tvos_sdk_version
flags.doc: Specifies the version of the tvOS SDK to use to build tvOS applications. If unspecified, uses default tvOS SDK version from 'xcode_version'.

flags.name: ui_actions_shown
flags.doc: Number of concurrent actions shown in the detailed progress bar; each action is shown on a separate line. The progress bar always shows at least one one, all numbers less than 1 are mapped to 1.

flags.name: ui_event_filters
flags.doc: Specifies which events to show in the UI. It is possible to add or remove events to the default ones using leading +/-, or override the default set completely with direct assignment. The set of supported event kinds include INFO, DEBUG, ERROR and more.

flags.name: unconditional_warning
flags.doc: A warning that will unconditionally get printed with build warnings and errors. This is useful to deprecate bazelrc files or --config definitions. If the intent is to effectively deprecate some flag or combination of flags, this is NOT sufficient. The flag or flags should use the deprecationWarning field in the option definition, or the bad combination should be checked for programmatically.

flags.name: universe_scope
flags.doc:
A comma-separated set of target patterns (additive and subtractive). The query may be performed in the universe defined by the transitive closure of the specified targets. This option is used for the query and cquery commands.
For cquery, the input to this option is the targets all answers are built under and so this option may affect configurations and transitions. If this option is not specified, the top-level targets are assumed to be the targets parsed from the query expression. Note: For cquery, not specifying this option may cause the build to break if targets parsed from the query expression are not buildable with top-level options.

flags.name: unix_digest_hash_attribute_name
flags.doc: The name of an extended attribute that can be placed on files to store a precomputed copy of the file's hash, corresponding with --digest_function. This option can be used to reduce disk I/O and CPU load caused by hash computation. This extended attribute is checked on all source files and output files, meaning that it causes a significant number of invocations of the getxattr() system call.

flags.name: unlimit_coredumps
flags.doc: Raises the soft coredump limit to the hard limit to make coredumps of the server (including the JVM) and the client possible under common conditions. Stick this flag in your bazelrc once and forget about it so that you get coredumps when you actually encounter a condition that triggers them.

flags.name: use_action_cache
flags.doc: Whether to use the action cache

flags.name: use_ijars
flags.doc: If enabled, this option causes Java compilation to use interface jars. This will result in faster incremental compilation, but error messages can be different.

flags.name: use_target_platform_for_tests
flags.doc: If true, then Bazel will use the target platform for running tests rather than the test exec group.

flags.name: use_top_level_targets_for_symlinks
flags.doc: Deprecated. No-op.

flags.name: vendor_dir
flags.doc: Specifies the directory that should hold the external repositories in vendor mode, whether for the purpose of fetching them into it or using them while building. The path can be specified as either an absolute path or a path relative to the workspace directory.

flags.name: verbose
flags.doc: The queries will also display the reason why modules were resolved to their current version (if changed). Defaults to true only for the explain query.

flags.name: verbose_explanations
flags.doc: Increases the verbosity of the explanations issued if --explain is enabled. Has no effect if --explain is not enabled.

flags.name: verbose_failures
flags.doc: If a command fails, print out the full command line.

flags.name: verbose_test_summary
flags.doc: If true, print additional information (timing, number of failed runs, etc) in the test summary.

flags.name: version_window_for_dirty_node_gc
flags.doc: Nodes that have been dirty for more than this many versions will be deleted from the graph upon the next update. Values must be non-negative long integers, or -1 indicating the maximum possible window.

flags.name: visionos_cpus
flags.doc: Comma-separated list of architectures for which to build Apple visionOS binaries.

flags.name: watchfs
flags.doc: If true, %{product} tries to use the operating system's file watch service for local changes instead of scanning every file for a change.

flags.name: watchos_cpus
flags.doc: Comma-separated list of architectures for which to build Apple watchOS binaries.

flags.name: watchos_minimum_os
flags.doc: Minimum compatible watchOS version for target simulators and devices. If unspecified, uses 'watchos_sdk_version'.

flags.name: watchos_sdk_version
flags.doc: Specifies the version of the watchOS SDK to use to build watchOS applications. If unspecified, uses default watchOS SDK version from 'xcode_version'.

flags.name: windows_enable_symlinks
flags.doc: If true, real symbolic links will be created on Windows instead of file copying. Requires Windows developer mode to be enabled and Windows 10 version 1703 or greater.

flags.name: worker_extra_flag
flags.doc: Extra command-flags that will be passed to worker processes in addition to --persistent_worker, keyed by mnemonic (e.g. --worker_extra_flag=Javac=--debug.

flags.name: worker_max_instances
flags.doc: How many instances of each kind of persistent worker may be launched if you use the 'worker' strategy. May be specified as [name=value] to give a different value per mnemonic. The limit is based on worker keys, which are differentiated based on mnemonic, but also on startup flags and environment, so there can in some cases be more workers per mnemonic than this flag specifies. Takes an integer, or a keyword ("auto", "HOST_CPUS", "HOST_RAM"), optionally followed by an operation ([-|*]<float>) eg. "auto", "HOST_CPUS*.5". 'auto' calculates a reasonable default based on machine capacity. "=value" sets a default for unspecified mnemonics.

flags.name: worker_max_multiplex_instances
flags.doc: How many WorkRequests a multiplex worker process may receive in parallel if you use the 'worker' strategy with --worker_multiplex. May be specified as [name=value] to give a different value per mnemonic. The limit is based on worker keys, which are differentiated based on mnemonic, but also on startup flags and environment, so there can in some cases be more workers per mnemonic than this flag specifies. Takes an integer, or a keyword ("auto", "HOST_CPUS", "HOST_RAM"), optionally followed by an operation ([-|*]<float>) eg. "auto", "HOST_CPUS*.5". 'auto' calculates a reasonable default based on machine capacity. "=value" sets a default for unspecified mnemonics.

flags.name: worker_multiplex
flags.doc: If enabled, workers will use multiplexing if they support it.

flags.name: worker_quit_after_build
flags.doc: If enabled, all workers quit after a build is done.

flags.name: worker_sandboxing
flags.doc: If enabled, workers will be executed in a sandboxed environment.

flags.name: worker_verbose
flags.doc: If enabled, prints verbose messages when workers are started, shutdown, ...

flags.name: workspace_directory
flags.doc: The root of the workspace, that is, the directory that Bazel uses as the root of the build. This flag is only to be set by the bazel client.

flags.name: workspace_rc
flags.doc: Whether or not to look for the workspace bazelrc file at $workspace/.bazelrc

flags.name: workspace_status_command
flags.doc: A command invoked at the beginning of the build to provide status information about the workspace in the form of key/value pairs.  See the User's Manual for the full specification. Also see tools/buildstamp/get_workspace_status for an example.

flags.name: write_command_log
flags.doc: Whether or not to write the command.log file

flags.name: xbinary_fdo
flags.doc: Use XbinaryFDO profile information to optimize compilation. Specify the name of default cross binary profile. When the option is used together with --fdo_instrument/--fdo_optimize/--fdo_profile, those options will always prevail as if xbinary_fdo is never specified.

flags.name: xcode_version
flags.doc: If specified, uses Xcode of the given version for relevant build actions. If unspecified, uses the executor default version of Xcode.

flags.name: xcode_version_config
flags.doc: The label of the xcode_config rule to be used for selecting the Xcode version in the build configuration.

flags.name: xml:default_values
flags.doc: If true, rule attributes whose value is not explicitly specified in the BUILD file are printed; otherwise they are omitted.

flags.name: xml:line_numbers
flags.doc: If true, XML output contains line numbers. Disabling this option may make diffs easier to read.  This option is only applicable to --output=xml.

flags.name: zip_undeclared_test_outputs
